ui_bugs.issue: No try/catch around api.post/api.put. When backend returns 409 (duplicate name), the axios error becomes an UNHANDLED promise rejection — no toast is shown to the user, dialog stays open silently, and in dev the webpack error overlay pops up ('Uncaught runtime errors: Request failed with status code 409'). Requirement says a duplicate customer must show an error toast.

Same as above — no try/catch around api.post('/products'). Duplicate product name → 409 → unhandled rejection, no toast, dev overlay blocks the UI. Requirement says duplicate product must show error toast.

issues: Radix warning: DialogContent missing DialogDescription/aria-describedby (pre-existing a11y warning, not blocking)

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/pages/Customers.js CustomerForm.save(), wrap the create/update calls in try/catch and show toast.error(errMsg(e)) on failure (mirror the pattern already used in Expenses.js).

In /app/frontend/src/pages/Inventory.js ProductForm.save() (and also CoilForm.save/adjust dialogs for consistency), wrap in try/catch and toast.error(errMsg(e)). Keep the dialog open so the user can correct the name.

critical_code_review_comments: Duplicate-guard error handling is missing on the two most user-visible create forms (Customers, Products). Backend correctly returns 409 but frontend swallows it as an unhandled rejection instead of surfacing a toast — exactly the UX the review request asked for.
Expenses.js correctly uses try { ... } catch (e) { toast.error(errMsg(e)); } — use it as the reference pattern for Customers and Inventory.

rca of the issue: Customers.js CustomerForm.save() and Inventory.js ProductForm.save() are `async` functions that call `await api.post(...)` without a try/catch. When the backend returns 409 for a duplicate name, axios rejects with AxiosError. Because save() is invoked directly from an onClick without a .catch(), the rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection — React dev-server's error overlay traps it and displays the full-screen 'Uncaught runtime errors: Request failed with status code 409'. In production the overlay would not appear but no toast would either, so the user would be left with a silent failure. Fix: wrap the body of save() in try/catch and call toast.error(errMsg(e)) on failure, mirroring Expenses.js. Also DO NOT call markSaved()/toast.success()/onClose() when the request throws — those currently sit after the await and would be reached only on success, so they are safe.
